# [STORY] As a maintainer, I want epic #30 and everything under it audited, so that "TMDB v3 API Clone Facade & Filmpire React App Integration" is accurate and test-backed

## User Story
**As a** maintainer
**I want** epic #30 and every story and task under it audited
**So that** "TMDB v3 API Clone Facade & Filmpire React App Integration" describes what was actually built, and every criterion is backed by a test or a re-runnable command

## Acceptance Criteria (Given/When/Then)
- [x] Given epic #30, when audited in epic mode, then it matches the epic template, meets the writing standard, and its native sub-issue links are complete and correct (`## Notes` corrected: #38/#44 were closed and re-parented under Stories #95/#98, the epic's own text no longer claims otherwise; sub-issues are exactly #91, #92)
- [x] Given story #91 and its 3 tasks, when its audit task below is done, then every one of them has been through the four gates (#274)
- [x] Given story #92 and its 3 tasks, when its audit task below is done, then every one of them has been through the four gates (#275)
- [x] Given every criterion in this subtree, when it is read, then it names a test, a CI step, or a re-runnable command, and none closes on a date (verified by hand across #30, #91, #92, #31, #32, #46, #33, #34, #47 — every criterion names a test, file, script, or `(manual: <steps>)`, at most one manual criterion per issue, no dates)
- [x] Given every issue in this subtree, when its metadata is read, then it has one type label, one priority label, no `sprint-N` label, and a correct native parent link (verified by hand across the same 9 issues)
- [x] Given every child story is audited, when epic #30 is checked, then it is closed if all its stories are closed, and left open otherwise (#91 and #92 are both closed; epic #30 is closed)

Scope: epic #30, its 2 stories, and the 6 tasks under them. Both child stories (#91, #92) were audited under #274 and #275. This run closed the remaining work: epic #30 in epic mode, and a Gate 3/4 pass across the whole subtree.

`infrastructure/scripts/audit-check.py` shells out to `gh`, which is not installed in this session's sandbox. Its checks (label/assignee/section/proof/date rules) were run by hand instead, reading each of the 9 issues in the subtree directly. No finding beyond the epic #30 Notes correction above.
